title.value: Tracking events become a real server-side no-op when tracking is disabled via config

description.value: Covers Controller/Track/Event.php's own early-return: 'if (!$this->config->isTrackingEnabled()) { return $result->setData(['ok' => false, 'reason' => 'tracking_disabled']); }' — every other tracking test in this suite assumes the config is already on (see StorefrontTrackerSetsVisitorCookieTest's own identical assumption note), this is the only one that flips it off and proves the endpoint itself refuses the event, not just that some downstream campaign never fires. Hits /ordo/track/event directly via a real fetch() from a real browser (not a magentoCLI call or a REST call) since this is exactly the endpoint window.ordoTrack() in view/frontend/web/js/tracker.js itself calls — the real client-side code path, not a simulated equivalent. Restores the config in the after-hook unconditionally: every other test in this same CI job/group assumes tracking is on, so leaving it off would be a real regression risk for whichever test happens to run next.

executeJS.function: window.__trackResult = undefined; fetch('/ordo/track/event', {method: 'POST', body: new URLSearchParams({visitor_id: 'disabled-tracking-test', event_type: 'page_view'})}).then(function (r) { return r.text(); }).then(function (text) { window.__trackResult = text; });
